Listening to an album start to finish rendered one tile per play, so the same cover repeated ten or more times in a row and the grid looked broken. Consecutive plays of one album now collapse into a single grid cell drawn as a stack of sleeves.

`groupAdjacentAlbumPlays` (new, tested) turns a section's plays into runs. **A run is a maximal set of temporally adjacent plays sharing an album ID** — purely positional, so the same album listened to twice in a day stays two stacks. Grouping runs over the accumulated track list inside each date section, which means a run straddling an infinite-scroll page boundary merges into one stack instead of splitting, and a run never spans "Today" into "This week" (a play belongs to exactly one section, so a merged stack would have to lie about when it happened).

`AlbumStack` (new) draws up to three sleeves — the run length hints at depth but never renders more than three. Sleeves share the front cover's border radius, card shadow, and bouncy hover transition, fan up and to the right with a slight tilt, and mix the page background into the sleeves behind so they recede in both light and dark. The whole stack is inscribed in its cell, so nothing collides with neighbours at any breakpoint. Hovering or focusing spreads the fan wider alongside the existing scale.

Follow-up to #572: the fade under the sticky music controls read as a hard band, and content scrolled through the uncovered strip between the bar and the top of the window.

**Content above the fade:** the bar sticks at the measured `--site-header-height`, so nothing ever covered the strip between it and the top of the viewport — album art scrolled right through it behind the glass header. `StickyFadeBar` now paints a viewport-anchored mask (`position: fixed; top: 0`, height `--site-header-height`) over that strip, so the masking region is separate from the control's own sticky offset. Fixed rather than absolute because an unpinned bar sits mid-page and only the top strip should ever be covered; fully opaque so a page with several bars paints the same pixels instead of stacking translucent copies.
**Harsh, long fade:** the trailing fade drops from `2.5rem` to `1.5rem` and now eases its alpha across five stops instead of ramping linearly, which is what made it read as a band.
Both changes live in the shared `StickyFadeBar`, so the albums sorter and the listening-history group headers pick them up from one place.

**Disappearing header:** Opening the footer music menu set MUI's scroll lock (`overflow: hidden` on `body`), which breaks `position: sticky`, so the header jumped to its document-flow position offscreen. Fixed with `disableScrollLock` on the menu. (Not a view-transition / `pinnedChromeSx` issue.)
